text.p: Conseco Inc, reporting improved third-quarter operating earnings, said Tuesday it plans further consolidation of its operations and the completion of certain pending acquisitions.
In 1997, the company plans to eliminate $10 million to $15 million in expenses from Life Partners Group, which it acquired on August 2.
"We also plan to consolidate American Life Holdings' operations from Des Moines, Iowa, into Carmel, Ind. by the middle of this month," said chairman Stephen Hilbert in a statement.
"This move will reduce American Life Holdings' annual operating expenses by approximately $10 million," he said. Conseco completed the American Life acquisition on September 20.

Hilbert also said he expects Conseco by yearend to complete the pending acquisitions of American Travellers Corp and Capitol American Financial Corp announced August 26, and the acquisition of Transport Holdings Inc announced September 26.
In addition, Hilbert said Conseco expects to complete the acquisition of the remaining 9.5 percent stake in Bankers Life Holding Corp by early January.

Following completion of these transactions, Hilbert said Conseco will have about $31 billion of investments under management, $27 billion of assets on its own balance sheet, $7 billion of annual premiums and revenues and $5.9 billion of equity market capitalization.
It also will have $690 million of projected EBIT (earnings before interest and taxes) cash flow and a book value of $33.50 per share, assuming conversion of its PRIDES securities.

Hilbert said Conseco directors and officers increased their direct ownership of the company's stock during the quarter. Insiders now hold about 24 percent of fully diluted shares outstanding, he noted.

Earlier Tuesday, Conseco reported third-quarter diluted operarting earnings of $1.01 per share, up from $0.72 per diluted share a year ago. It said results beat the street consensus of $0.94 for operating earnings per fully diluted share.
